scope: Read-only peer assessment of the approved literal surface, not mathematical proof fills or an external gate verdict

definitions.name: Complexity.padSAT
definitions.restatement: A bit word belongs when it has a satisfiable prefix, then one false separator, then exactly the prefix length raised to its chosen length-dependent exponent many true bits.
definitions.checks: The separator makes the prefix strictly shorter even at exponent0 or empty prefix. Last-false parsing is unambiguous because the suffix is all true. Inherited malformed-input SAT membership is preserved, not replaced by a well-formedness premise.
definitions.approved_convention: LD3 literal padding; own mem_padSAT_iff and padSAT_congr give the readings.

definitions.name: Complexity.ladnerMachine
definitions.restatement: Interpret the natural index's binary digits using the existing uniformly timed machine-code scheme, then take its binary finite-machine realization.
definitions.checks: The equation reader does not establish coverage or infinitely many arbitrarily large indices. Those normal-form/code-padding facts remain explicit mathematical fill obligations.
definitions.approved_convention: LD1 uniform expCode enumeration, not unbounded per-code simulation constants.

definitions.name: Complexity.ladnerH
definitions.restatement: At length n, test indices below the floor double logarithm against acceptance of the padded language on all words up to the floor logarithm, using deadline i times the word length to the power i. Return the least successful index, or the cap if none succeeds; the recursion uses already defined smaller exponent values.
definitions.checks: padSAT_congr and the strict decrease of queried prefix lengths justify the proved global equation. Zero is handled separately. The definition makes no monotonicity claim and does not require total Boolean output at the zero deadline.
definitions.approved_convention: LD2 acceptance equivalence, LD4 floor logs, LD5 strong recursion/least-index fallback.

definitions.name: Complexity.SAT_H
definitions.restatement: Use ladnerH as the variable exponent in padSAT.
definitions.checks: This is the explicit witness language, not an independently assumed arbitrary intermediate language. Conditional nonemptiness examples require their SAT witness, as recorded.
definitions.approved_convention: LD7 explicit witness plus existential packaging.

mathematical_targets.name: Complexity.ladnerH_polyTime
mathematical_targets.literal_assessment: Expected polynomial computability of the binary H value on the input length. There are polynomially many short test words; capped indices and their numeric deadlines admit a polynomial envelope, and smaller H values can be memoized. Concrete preparation, uniform simulator cost, sharp SAT search and memo-state ledgers are still obligations. No conditional host probe is promoted to those missing premises.

mathematical_targets.name: Complexity.SAT_H_mem_NP
mathematical_targets.literal_assessment: Expected from the polynomial H computation plus guessing/checking a SAT prefix certificate and its exactly prescribed suffix. An oversized exponent can be handled with bounded length comparison rather than writing its huge power. The existing total SAT convention must be carried through the verifier; no missing well-formedness hypothesis is silently added.

mathematical_targets.name: Complexity.ladnerH_bounded_of_mem_P
mathematical_targets.literal_assessment: A polynomial decider should have a sufficiently large padded enumeration index dominating its degree and coefficient; that index eventually passes all bounded tests, giving a uniform cap with finitely many initial exceptions. The infinite-index/normal-form fact is not supplied by ladnerMachine_eq. Empty-input acceptance is false on both sides, so the zero deadline does not invalidate this argument.

mathematical_targets.name: Complexity.ladnerH_unbounded_of_not_mem_P
mathematical_targets.literal_assessment: If the language is outside P, each fixed indexed polynomial-clock acceptance test must have some finite counterexample. Once all counterexamples below a fixed index and a large enough cap are visible, no such index can be chosen. The conclusion is eventual divergence, stronger than mere unboundedness; no monotonicity is needed.

mathematical_targets.name: Complexity.SAT_mem_P_of_padSAT_NPHard
mathematical_targets.literal_assessment: A polynomial reduction into an eventually highly padded language yields a much shorter candidate SAT prefix for large outputs; finite small prefixes can be tabulated and recursive shrinking gives a polynomial SAT procedure. Polynomial-time binary exponent evaluation supports exact padding checks. NP membership of the target is not used by that shrinking argument, so NPHard is the declared weaker premise/stronger theorem. Tail divergence is essential; mere spikes of large h are insufficient.

mathematical_targets.name: Complexity.SAT_H_intermediate
mathematical_targets.literal_assessment: Under P≠NP, membership follows from the NP target. A P decider would bound H and make bounded padding reduce SAT to the witness, collapsing P and NP. NP-hardness would combine the non-P divergence claim with the shrinking theorem to give the same collapse. The bounded-padding reduction is a local fill obligation, not an unapproved seventh public theorem.

packaging.name: Complexity.ladner
packaging.assessment: The explicit witness theorem immediately supplies the existential theorem; its AX contains sorryAx transitively. It is not an independently proved Ladner theorem.

logical_adversarial_cases_not_new_native: At empty prefix, 0^0=1 if the exponent is0; at positive exponent the unary suffix may be empty. The mandatory false separator still excludes the empty padded word.
At i=0 every indexed deadline is0, including empty input. The public zero-time obstruction makes acceptance false; total-output correctness at that clock is deliberately not asserted.
H(0)=H(1)=0 is actually checked by the six-edge evidence. Caps at4 and16 are1 and2; which positive indices pass remains a machine-specific test, not an extra claimed executed result.
A malformed SAT prefix is interpreted by the existing total decoder. An all-true output word nevertheless has no padding separator and cannot belong to padSAT.
A nonmonotone but eventually diverging exponent satisfies the general theorem's tail premise; an exponent with arbitrarily large spikes but infinitely many zeros does not.
source_edition_limit: The recorded LD8 fallback authorizes Theorem3.3/proof citations while exact2009 exercise-part wording is unverified. This peer checks that faithful declaration of limits and the approved conventions; it does not claim an independent2009 book-page verification.
